cards.text: When Jesus sees the crowds, He goes up on the mountain and sits down, and His disciples come to Him. Then He begins to teach them. Friend, when I sit down in my bakery, it's because my gold base tipped over and took me with it.
His very first word? BLESSED. "Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven."
Next, Jesus calls those who mourn blessed. When I mourned in that junk drawer, the rubber bands I shared it with didn't call me blessed, friend, they called me "the guy who keeps SIGHING."

cards.question: Jesus promises those who mourn that they will be comforted.
Jesus' first two lines about the poor in spirit and those who mourn are built the same way. What's the pattern?

answers.text: Who is blessed and what they'll get
What to do and what to avoid
A question and then its answer

cards.text: Then Jesus says the meek are blessed, for they will inherit the earth. Friend, I'm not even meek with my oven timer, and the timer WINS every single time.
Next, Jesus calls blessed those who hunger and thirst for righteousness. That's not a craving for cookies, friend, that's a craving for what's right.

cards.question: Jesus says those who hunger and thirst for righteousness will be ___.
Jesus calls the merciful blessed and promises them the very thing they give out.

cards.text: Then Jesus names the next group who are blessed, for they will see God, and He describes them by their hearts. Friend, MY heart is about 40 percent love and 60 percent butterscotch bits.

cards.question: Jesus says the ___ in heart are blessed, for they will see God.

cards.text: Then Jesus names another group who are blessed, and He says they will be called sons of God.

cards.question: Jesus says one group will be called sons of God. Who are they?

cards.text: Peacemakers, friend. I shared a junk drawer with dead batteries that argued over who had the most charge left, so I KNOW making peace is hard work.

cards.question: Jesus also calls blessed those who are persecuted. What does He say they're persecuted because of?
Jesus promises those persecuted because of righteousness the same thing He promised the poor in spirit.

cards.text: Then Jesus switches from 'those' to 'you': "Blessed are you when people insult you, persecute you, and falsely say all kinds of evil against you because of Me."

cards.question: People insult and persecute them because of Jesus. What does Jesus tell them to do?
Jesus says they can rejoice when they're persecuted because of Him, because great is their reward in ___.
Jesus says His listeners will be the first people ever persecuted this way.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, "You are the salt of the earth." Friend, back in that junk drawer, the most anybody ever called me was "Hey, what's this thing?"
But then Jesus asks: if the salt loses its savor, how can it be made salty again? Sounds like a stamper losing its edges, friend, and you KNOW I've been there.

cards.question: What does Jesus say happens to salt that loses its savor?

answers.text: It's dried out in the sun

cards.text: Then Jesus paints a new picture: "You are the light of the world." Friend, I spent years in a dark drawer begging for one slice of kitchen light, and Jesus is talking about the WHOLE WORLD.

cards.question: Jesus says a city on a hill can be hidden if it tries hard enough.
Jesus says people don't light a lamp and put it under a basket. Where does He say they set it?

cards.text: Up on the stand, it gives light to everyone in the house. And Jesus says that in the same way, His listeners should let their light shine before men.

cards.question: When their light shines before men, Jesus says people will see their good ___.
When people see those good deeds, who does Jesus say they'll glorify?

cards.text: That's where we'll stop for now, and Mags would be ringing LOUD for this one. Keep that apron on, friend, because Jesus is NOT done teaching.

findings.problem: The second sentence spends the card's words defining 'righteousness' as 'a craving for what's right' instead of moving the sermon along. The dictionary pop-up covers the word.

rule.text: Don't spend card words explaining a hard word. Hard words get a dictionary pop-up (definitions.md, made after the cards).

findings.problem: The card is one flat sentence of narration with none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The card tells no new part of the passage. It repeats 'Peacemakers' after card 13 has already answered it, only to set up a joke. That makes it a recap and joke-only card, not a step forward through the sermon.

rule.text:
Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.
- No recap cards.
- When the story continues. ...
- Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The joke invents a new drawer moment: the rubber bands nicknaming him 'the guy who keeps SIGHING.' Stop 2 card 5 does the same with someone calling him 'Hey, what's this thing?' papa-dorin.md says he never adds anything new to his world, and that jokes can make up small moments 'around his bakery.' It doesn't say whether that allowance also covers the junk drawer, even though he 'laughs at his days in the drawer.'
findings.question: Can Papa Dorin's jokes make up small new moments from his junk drawer days, or only around his bakery?

findings.problem: The question says 'People insult and persecute them' without saying who 'them' is. The story card that set up 'you' is no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'they're persecuted' and 'their reward' don't say who is being persecuted. Like card 2, it leans on a card that is no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: No card ever tells that Jesus says the prophets were persecuted the same way (Matthew 5:12). The false answer only shows that the listeners aren't the first. The comparison with the prophets is an important detail that the walkthrough leaves out.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: 'When their light shines' doesn't say whose light. The story card that named Jesus' listeners is no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'those good deeds' points back to card 12, which is no longer on screen. The right answer 'Their Father in heaven' is also unclear, because 'their' could mean the people watching instead of Jesus' listeners.
